findings.location: #s3-wizard, <div> container, style order property reverses steps, lines 47-57
findings.evidence: DOM order: Step 3 (order:3), Step 2 (order:2), Step 1 (order:1); visual/CSS order: Step 1, Step 2, Step 3
findings.violation: Steps appear in reversed order to screen readers; linearized reading presents confirm step before entry step, reversing the checkout sequence
findings.fix: Reorder DOM to match visual order: choose plan first, then payment, then confirm; or remove order property and adjust visual CSS differently

findings.evidence: Custom div element with img child (trash icon), no role, no aria-label, no onclick handler visible in markup
findings.violation: Custom control lacks role, accessible name, and state; appears intended as delete button but exposes nothing to assistive technology
findings.fix: Add role="button" (or role="menuitem" if part of a menu), add aria-label="Delete", add click handler with keyboard support (Enter/Space), or use native <button> element

findings.evidence: Label styled with color:#cc0000 (red); no asterisk, no "required" attribute, no other non-color signal present
findings.violation: Color alone signals required status; color-blind reader cannot distinguish this field from optional fields
findings.fix: Add visible required indicator: append " *" text, or add aria-required="true" with CSS-generated asterisk, or add "(required)" text

findings.evidence: Error message reads "Error." with no indication of field name or problem type
findings.violation: Error text is generic and does not identify which field failed or why; reader must guess the issue
findings.fix: Replace "Error." with specific message: e.g., "Promo code not found" or "Promo code expired"; or prepend field name: "Promo code: invalid format"
